exposure: Historic cohort (immediate cord clamping), DCC cohort (delayed cord clamping for 60 seconds)
cohort: 62 very preterm infants born from twin deliveries between 23(0/7) and 31(6/7) weeks gestation
finding: Delayed cord clamping in very preterm twins was safe, feasible, and associated with a significant reduction in early red blood cell transfusions but not with any adverse neonatal outcomes compared to early cord clamping.
mod_finding: The study found that delayed cord clamping in very preterm twins was not associated with adverse neonatal outcomes compared to early cord clamping.
